text:
support_engineer_kyle: heads up — customer SUP-3421 (ABC Corp) opened a ticket: sudden p95/p99 regression for short prompt workloads on the continuous-batcher profile since yesterday ~03:00 UTC. p99 jumped from ~120ms to ~2.3s. They sent traces showing many requests stuck in "hold" for ~1.8s.
samir: thanks. any config changes deployed near that time?
support_engineer_kyle: ops notes show a config rollout 02:55 UTC that changed continuous-batcher: max_hold_ms 500 -> 200 and min_batch_size 1 -> 2 for the profile used by abc corp. Link to rollout: https://console.internal/rollouts/rollout-879
alex_chen: wow lowering max_hold_ms should reduce latency not increase it. but min_batch_size bump could cause queues to wait longer for small-concurrency clients. maybe tiny-requests starved until timeout triggered.
maria_g: I pulled metrics from grafana: query: 
```
sum(rate(requests_total{profile="continuous-batcher",tenant="abc-corp"}[1m])) by (instance)
```
and tail latency: 
```
histogram_quantile(0.99, sum(rate(request_duration_seconds_bucket{profile="continuous-batcher",tenant="abc-corp"}[5m])) by (le))
```
p99 trace shows a cluster at ~1.9s and another around 200-300ms.
irene_ops: Also saw an increase in "batch_hold_time_ms" metric distribution after rollout. Export from 03:00-04:00 shows 75th=120ms, 95th=1.6s.
samir: ok repro plan: can we replay a small-concurrency short-request load against a canary with the new config? alex, can you spin a test route with the abc-corp profile?
alex_chen: creating a canary now: `rbctl rollout create --profile continuous-batcher --overrides '{"min_batch_size":2,"max_hold_ms":200}' --target canary-test-abc`
deploy-bot: deploy started for rollout canary-test-abc by alex_chen at 2419823348
opsbot: note: automatically applied batching override to route `api/abc/v1/generate` at 02:55 UTC (rollout-id: 879)
support_engineer_kyle: customer supplied a minimal repro: many parallel clients each sending 1-3 token prompts every ~150ms. sample curl: 
```
curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood/test-generate -H "Authorization: Bearer <redacted>" -d '{"model":"xlarge","input":"hi","max_tokens":8}'
```
samir: that pattern will produce a lot of tiny batches. With min_batch_size=2 the worker will wait to reach batch size before dispatching, so if arrivals are spaced ~150ms it waits until either size or max_hold_ms, causing tail.
maria_g: interesting — lowering max_hold_ms to 200ms should have reduced hold but if earlier config change ALSO decreased concurrency or changed batching shuffle, maybe some requests get delayed due to hold-window jitter + GC spikes. check GC/CPU around 03:00.
alex_chen: can confirm a GC surge on node batcher-17 at 02:58 UTC. logs: 
```
[02:58:01] INFO gc: pause 1.2s heap=1.4G
[02:58:02] WARN batcher: held 28 requests waiting for batch size=2 for 1200ms
```
irene_ops: So root cause hypothesis: combo of min_batch_size bump + transient GC on a subset of batcher pods created long tail. tiny requests that hit the affected pod experienced hold-time amplified.
support_engineer_kyle: customer asked for an immediate mitigation — they need stable p99 under 300ms. what's the fastest safe change?
samir: immediate mitigation options: 1) Temporarily lower min_batch_size back to 1 for that tenant/profile (fast config flip) 2) Increase max_hold_ms? no, that would worsen p99. 3) Route ABC tenant to a small-batch profile that uses single-request flush. I'd do #1 + create small-batch profile for longer-term.
alex_chen: filed canary change: `rbctl rollout update canary-test-abc --overrides '{"min_batch_size":1}'`
deploy-bot: rollout canary-test-abc updated by alex_chen at 2419823354 — starting canary validation
opsbot: metric alert suppressed for abc-corp p99 during canary window per SOP (ticket SUP-3421)
maria_g: while canary runs, run the repro script against canary endpoint: 
```
./repro_small_prompts.sh --endpoint https://canary.api.redwood/test-generate --clients 40 --rate 6
```
support_engineer_kyle: ran it — p99 dropped to 220ms, p95 95ms. customer confirmed latency improved in their staging.
irene_ops: follow-ups: we should audit other profiles for recent min_batch_size changes, and add a histogram of `batch_hold_time_ms` per-tenant to surface this earlier. also add a safety-rule: never set min_batch_size>1 when avg request size tokens < 8 and per-tenant qps < 10.
samir: Agreed. Propose longer-term fixes: adaptive hold timeout per-tenant (based on arrival distribution), and a small-batch bypass for short-prompt/high-sparsity workloads. Also add auto-eviction from batcher pod if GC pause > 500ms to avoid amplified hold.
alex_chen: I'll open follow-up RFC and a monitoring dashboard. RFC: RFD-118: Adaptive batching heuristics.
support_engineer_kyle: Next steps for the customer: 1) applied rollback (min_batch_size=1) 2) monitoring patch deployed 3) ops will keep canary for 24h then promote. Informing customer now — they asked for root cause and mitigation.
deploy-bot: canary validation succeeded. promoting canary to 20% traffic at 2419823366
opsbot: ticket SUP-3421 updated: mitigation applied, RCA in progress.
maria_g: one more note — add a quick runbook blurb: when p99 spikes for continuous-batcher with short prompts, check min_batch_size and batch_hold_time_ms, and consider tenant-level override to small-batch profile before broad rollback.
support_engineer_kyle: thanks team — I'll post summary to customer and link this thread. if anyone wants ownership of RFC RFD-118 ping me. :thumbsup:
